issues.t: Air suspension strut leaks and the car sags
issues.sym: One corner or end of the car sits low, often after being parked overnight. You may see a suspension or stability warning, hear the air compressor running a lot, or feel tires rubbing the wheel wells. In bad cases the car drops while driving.
issues.why: The Equus rides on air struts, which use rubber air bags instead of coil springs. Those bags and their seals wear and start leaking, usually somewhere between about 50,000 and 135,000 miles. A leak makes the compressor overwork and can burn it out too. Suspension is the most-reported problem on this car.
issues.next: If the car is sitting very low or the tires rub, don't drive it; have it towed. Otherwise get the air system leak-tested soon. Ask for the ride-height sensors to be recalibrated after any strut replacement. Some owners convert to conventional struts.

issues.t: Brake pedal sinks and braking feels weak
issues.sym: The brake pedal goes much closer to the floor than normal and the car takes longer to stop. Warning lights for the brakes or stability control may come on.
issues.why: The hydraulic brake control unit (HECU, the ABS and stability control pump) can fail inside. Hyundai extended the warranty on this unit for 2011-2012 Equus to 15 years with unlimited miles, and issued a bulletin about replacing the brake fluid on early cars.
issues.next: Treat a sinking pedal as urgent. Leave lots of room and get it checked before driving more. Ask a Hyundai or Genesis dealer to check the extended HECU warranty for your VIN, since owners report this is a major repair.

issues.t: ABS module can leak inside and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Often no warning. Possible signs are an ABS warning light, a burning smell, or brake fluid around the ABS unit under the hood.
issues.why: Brake fluid can leak inside the anti-lock brake module and short its electronics, which can start a fire under the hood even when the car is parked. Recall 23V-651 adds a new ABS fuse. Owners reported waiting months for parts.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 23V-651. Until it is done, park outside and away from buildings. If you smell burning or see smoke, pull over, turn the car off and get away from it.

issues.sym: Wipers work on and off, park in odd spots, or stop completely, sometimes in the middle of a rainstorm.
issues.why: The seal on the wiper motor cover breaks down and lets water in, which corrodes the motor's circuit board. Recall 16V-117 replaces the cover and seal on Equus built from July 2011 to June 2012. Hyundai also extended the wiper motor warranty to 10 years or 100,000 miles on 2011-2013 Equus.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 16V-117. If the wipers act up, don't drive in rain or snow until they are fixed, and ask the dealer whether the extended motor warranty applies.

issues.t: Brake lights may not come on (recall)
issues.sym: The brake lights don't light when you press the pedal, or work only when the headlights are on. Drivers behind you may not know you are stopping.
issues.why: A fault in the stop-lamp switch circuit can keep the brake lights off. Recall 14V-713 repairs the circuit.
issues.next: Have someone watch the brake lights while you press the pedal. Check your VIN for recall 14V-713 and get it fixed promptly, since a rear-end crash is the risk.

issues.t: Engine shuts off or hesitates while driving
issues.sym: The car suddenly loses power or shuts off at highway speed, the gas pedal stops responding for a few seconds, or acceleration drops while cruise control is on. Steering and brakes feel heavy during the shutdown.
issues.why: Owners report this across 2013-2016 models, often with no warning light. Dealers frequently could not reproduce it, so the cause varies from car to car.
issues.next: If it happens, steer to the shoulder and turn on your hazards. Note when it happens and any messages on the dash, and have a dealer read stored codes. Report it to NHTSA if the dealer finds nothing.

issues.t: Rod bearing knock and engine failure
issues.sym: A deep knocking from the engine that gets louder with speed, low oil pressure, or the engine seizing, sometimes without any warning light first.
issues.why: Owners of 2011 and 2014 models report rod bearing failure and seized engines. Hyundai issued a bulletin (21-EM-004H) on testing connecting rod bearing clearance on its engines. Low or overdue oil makes bearing wear worse.
issues.next: If you hear knocking, stop driving and check the oil level. Have the car towed to a dealer and ask whether any Hyundai engine coverage or bulletin applies to your VIN.

issues.sym: Clunky or jolting shifts, a pause before the car picks up a gear, engine revs flaring between gears, or a check engine light with transmission codes.
issues.why: Hyundai issued several bulletins for these transmissions: replacing shift solenoids for harsh or flaring upshifts, replacing the transmission's electronic module for certain codes instead of the whole transmission, and reloading pressure data so it relearns shifts.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the fluid level checked using Hyundai's procedure. Ask the shop to check the bulletins before agreeing to replace the transmission.

issues.sym: Revs rise without the car speeding up, a check engine light with an 'incorrect ratio' code, or the car feeling like it slips out of gear.
issues.why: Worn clutches inside the automatic transmission let it slip. Hyundai has bulletins on stall-testing these transmissions and on diagnosing incorrect-ratio codes before replacement.
issues.next: Avoid hard acceleration and get it diagnosed soon. Slipping usually gets worse and can leave you stranded.

issues.t: Headlights and turn signals cut out
issues.sym: Headlights, turn signals or interior lights flicker or go dark for several seconds, sometimes at highway speed at night, often in AUTO headlight mode.
issues.why: Owners report intermittent lighting faults that dealers often can't reproduce. RepairPal also lists headlight flickering as a common Equus problem.
issues.next: If the lights go out at night, slow down, turn on your hazards and get off the road safely. Have the lighting circuits and modules checked, and take a video of it happening to show the dealer.

issues.t: Active headrest pops up or cracks
issues.sym: A front headrest suddenly snaps forward with a bang, splits open or crumbles, while driving or parked, with no crash.
issues.why: The active headrests are spring-loaded to move forward in a rear crash. Owners report the trigger firing on its own or the headrest housing breaking.
issues.next: Have the headrest inspected and reset or replaced. A headrest stuck forward or broken won't protect your neck properly in a crash.

issues.t: Airbag light from a failed clock spring
issues.sym: The airbag warning light comes on, and the horn or steering wheel buttons may stop working.
issues.why: The clock spring is a coiled ribbon cable in the steering column that connects the driver airbag and wheel buttons. Hyundai extended its warranty to 15 years with unlimited miles under bulletin 21-BE-003H-1.
issues.next: The driver airbag may not work while this light is on. Ask a Hyundai or Genesis dealer to check the extended clock spring coverage for your VIN.

issues.t: Car pulls or alignment won't stay in spec
issues.sym: The car drifts to one side on a straight road or the steering wheel sits off-center, even after an alignment.
issues.why: Hyundai issued a bulletin (TSB-11-SS-004) for a tracking condition on these cars. Owners report shops being unable to set the alignment to specification.
issues.next: Have tire pressures and wear checked first. Then ask a dealer to follow the tracking bulletin rather than just doing a standard alignment.

issues.t: Leather dashboard cover shrinking or lifting
issues.sym: The leather on the dashboard pulls away from its base, bubbles or wrinkles, especially in hot weather.
issues.why: The stitched leather dash cover shrinks over time with heat. Fixing it means removing the windshield and dashboard, so it is a major repair.
issues.next: This is cosmetic unless the cover starts lifting near the windshield or airbag area. Get quotes from an auto upholstery shop as well as the dealer, and use a windshield sunshade to slow it down.

issues.sym: A window stops going up or down, or sticks partway, sometimes more often in hot weather.
issues.why: Owners report window motors dying around 48,000 miles, with one owner on a third motor in under two years.
issues.next: If a window is stuck open, cover it and get it fixed before rain. Replacement parts sometimes have to be ordered, so plan for a short wait.

issues.sym: Fog or water droplets inside a headlight, taillight, fog light or daytime running light, sometimes followed by bulbs or LEDs failing.
issues.why: Hyundai has bulletins (20-BD-014H and 23-BD-002H) on condensation in its lamps. Some light fogging after washing can be normal, but standing water means a seal has failed.
issues.next: If the fog clears on its own after driving, it is usually harmless. If water pools inside, have the lamp resealed or replaced before it damages the wiring.

issues.sym: Heavy black soot coats the rear bumper and trunk lid around the tailpipes and is hard to clean off.
issues.why: Owners of 2016 models report it. Heavy soot means the engine is burning rich or building carbon, which can come from injector, sensor or ignition problems.
issues.next: Have the engine checked for codes, misfires and fuel trim. Ongoing heavy soot can damage the catalytic converters.
